simple: This page is about `AngularVelocity`, a constraint that keeps a part spinning at a steady speed. Physics adds just enough twisting force to keep the spin the same. It is handy for spinning platforms, fans, windmills, and obstacle course spinners. You can also choose whether the spin is measured against the world or against another attachment.
analogy: It is like a record player motor: no matter if you lightly touch the record, the motor keeps it turning at the same steady speed.
keyPoints: `AngularVelocity` applies torque (twisting force) to an assembly to keep a constant spin speed.
If you want to choose the amount of twist instead of the spin speed, use a `Torque` constraint.
If you only want a part to start spinning once, set its `AssemblyAngularVelocity` directly instead.
The `RelativeTo` property controls how the spin is measured.
With `RelativeTo` set to `World`, the spin vector is used exactly as you typed it.
With `RelativeTo` set to `Attachment1`, the spin is added on top of whatever the other attachment's part is doing, so a part on a spinning base spins with it.

terms.constraint: An object that controls how parts move, like an invisible motor, rope, or hand pushing them. Mover constraints push or spin parts for you.
terms.assembly: A group of parts that are welded or joined together so physics moves them as one piece. A car body plus its welded seats is one assembly.
terms.attachment: A small invisible point you put inside a part. Constraints hook onto attachments, the same way a rope ties onto a hook.
terms.Attachment0 / Attachment1: The two attachment slots a constraint uses. Attachment0 is usually the one that gets pushed; Attachment1 is the other end or the reference point.
terms.angular velocity: How fast something spins and around which axis. (0, 5, 0) means spinning around the up axis at 5 radians per second.
terms.torque: A twisting push that makes things spin, like turning a doorknob or a wrench.
terms.radian: A way to measure angles. A full circle is about 6.28 radians, so 6.28 radians per second is about one full turn each second.
terms.axis: The invisible line something spins around. A merry-go-round spins around a straight up-and-down axis.
terms.reaction torque: An equal twist in the opposite direction applied to the other part, like how your body twists back when you spin a heavy wheel.

example.title: Make a spinning platform
example.place: Script inside a Part in Workspace (part not Anchored, and held in place by a hinge or kept from falling)
example.code:
local part = script.Parent

local attachment = Instance.new("Attachment")
attachment.Parent = part

local spinner = Instance.new("AngularVelocity")
spinner.Attachment0 = attachment
spinner.RelativeTo = Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo.World
spinner.AngularVelocity = Vector3.new(0, 3, 0) -- spin around the up (Y) axis
spinner.MaxTorque = math.huge -- allow as much twist as needed
spinner.Parent = part
explain: We add an `Attachment` so the constraint has something to act on.
We create an `AngularVelocity` and connect it with `Attachment0`.
`AngularVelocity = (0, 3, 0)` means spin around the Y axis (straight up) at 3 radians per second, a bit less than half a turn each second.
`MaxTorque = math.huge` lets it twist as hard as needed to hold that speed.
Parenting it to the part starts the spinning.

watchOut: An unanchored spinning part will also fall from gravity. Hold it with a hinge or other constraint if it should stay in one place.
Spin speeds are in radians per second, not degrees. 360 would be extremely fast; try small numbers like 1 to 5.
If `MaxTorque` is too low, a heavy part will spin slower than you asked.
